complaint: Email sends looked really slow starting the morning of March 9th. Someone said it was probably the sender deploy that day. Never confirmed.

response.restated_complaint: The engineer is asking whether email sends were slow starting the morning of March 9th, and whether the comms-sender deploy that day was the cause.

hypotheses.summary: Email sends did slow down starting 2026-03-09T09:00:00.755Z: 6 sends degraded to 4120ms vs a 235ms baseline (17.5x), all hitting provider 429 (rate-limited) responses with 18 retries before eventually succeeding (final status 202) — so nothing was lost, but latency spiked for about a day. The suspected cause, the comms-sender deploy c52a0f9 (PR #99, 'Add SMS provider seam') at 14:00 that day, is explicitly ruled out: it postdates the onset of the slowdown by 5 hours, and 3 of the 6 affected messages had already occurred before it deployed. The data cannot determine what actually ended the incident — it recovered by 2026-03-10T11:13, and a different sender deploy, e18d773 (PR #101, 'Bump provider SDK') at 2026-03-10T10:00, landed right inside that recovery window.
hypotheses.why_this_rank: This is the only finding that matches both the timing (starting the morning of March 9th) and the nature (email slowness) of the complaint, and it directly addresses and rules out the suspected sender deploy from that day.

ruled_out.claim: The comms-sender deploy c52a0f9 (PR #99, deployed 2026-03-09T14:00:00Z) caused the email slowdown.
ruled_out.why_not: The slowdown began at 2026-03-09T09:00:00.755Z, 5 hours before this deploy, and 3 of the 6 affected messages had already occurred before it went out.

would_resolve: the e18d773 diff — if PR #101 changed connection pooling, concurrency, or retry configuration, the client-side hypothesis (H2) gains weight; if it was a version bump with no client-behaviour change, the provider-side hypothesis (H1) does
provider-side account rate-limit metrics for the incident window
whether other producers on the shared quota saw the same throttling around 2026-03-09/10
